AGENDA
  GLENDALE WATER AND POWER COMMISSION
  (STAFF ACCESS ONLY) GLENDALE WATER AND POWER DEPARTMENT
  633 E. Broadway, Room 105 (MSB 105)
  Glendale, CA 91206
 Welcome to the meeting of the Glendale Water and Power Commission. Meetings are broadcast live
 on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program
 schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office. Meetings
 are  also  archived  on  the  City  Website  for  viewing  anytime  at
 https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal. If you have any question about
 matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the Glendale Water and Power
 Administration Office at (818) 548-2107 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Glendale Water and Power Administration Office,
 141 N. Glendale Ave., Suite 450, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  AUGUST 3, 2020 AT 4:00 PM

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department, the Glendale Water and Power Commission meeting will be
available to the public electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:
On local cable: Charter Cable Channel 6 and AT&T U-verse Channel 99.
Streaming Online: https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal

  1
 For public comments and questions during the meeting call (818) 937-8100.

City staff will be submitting these questions and comments in real time to the appropriate person
during the Glendale Water and Power Commission meeting.

1.  ROLL CALL – 4:00 PM
2.  CONSENT ITEMS – (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
  Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.
  a. Approval of the July 6, 2020 Meeting Minutes
3.  GWP COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
4.  REPORTS - INFORMATION
  a. Legislative Update
  b. Customer Services Update
  c. Annual Water Quality Report
  d. Scholl Biogas Project Update
5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS (5) Minutes
  Discussion is limited to items NOT part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five (5)
  minutes – Commission may question or respond to the speaker, but there will be no debate or
  decision. The General Manager may refer the matter to appropriate staff for investigation and
  report.
6.  AGENDA FORECAST
  a. Agenda Forecast
7.  ADJOURNMENT

MINUTES
  GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  MUNICIPAL SERVICES BUILDING
  633 E. Broadway, 1st Floor, Room 105 - Glendale, CA 91206

  Monday, August 3, 2020, 4:00 PM

1. ROLL CALL
  The meeting was called to order at 4:04 p.m.

  Present: Commissioners Lall, Flanigan, and Jazmadarian

  Absent: President Kedikian, Commissioner Avanessian

2. CONSENT ITEMS
  a. Approval of the July 6, 2020 Meeting Minutes
  The Commission approved the minutes as published.

3. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  None.

4. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. Legislative Update.
  Mr. Leo Zalyan, Administrative Analyst, presented the legislative update. Mr. Zalyan
  provided information relating to the 2020 legislative calendar. Mr. Zalyan provided
  information regarding the 2020 Budget Act signed by Governor Newsom, which is aimed
  to strengthen emergency response, protect public health and safety, and promote
  economic recovery. Mr. Zalyan summarized the key energy bills and water bills.

  Commissioner Flanigan inquired regarding the key energy bills relating to microgrids and
  the size-cap and whether it is still 1 megawatt per customer. Mr. Zalyan and Mr. Steve
  Zurn, General Manager, explained that the next cycle's cap would be decided at the next
  legislative cycle.

  Commissioner Lall inquired whether GWP has taken a position (in support or opposition)
  of any legislation for the current session. Mr. Zalyan explained that GWP has not taken
  any formal positions and that it is tracking the bills along with CMUA and SCPPA.

  b. Customer Services Update.
  Ms. Tami Vallier, Customer Services Administrator, presented the customer services
  update. Ms. Vallier provided an update relating to COVID-19 impacts. Ms. Vallier
  summarized GWP’s efforts amidst COVID-19, which included closing customer service
  counters, sending customers pre-recorded messages and connecting vis social media;
  processing payments through drop boxes, pay-near-me stations located in 7-eleven
  stores, on-line payments, and payment over the telephone. Ms. Vallier explained a
  1
   moratorium on utility disconnections/shut-offs due to non-payment through the end of the
  calendar year 2020. Additionally, there is a suspension of late fees through the end of the
  calendar year 2020. Ms. Vallier also discussed the CARES Bill relief program
  implemented by GWP for its customers affected by COVID-19.

  Commissioner Flanigan stated that he was impressed that GWP was able to pivot so
  quickly due to COVID-19. Commissioner Flanigan commented whether post-COVID-19,
  GWP will continue utilizing some of the remote services.

  Commissioner Jazmadarian inquired regarding how much funds have been spent to date
  in the CARES program. Ms. Atineh Haroutunian explained that the cap for the program is
  $3 million, and GWP customers have until October 1, 2020, to submit applications. Mr.
  Zurn explained that GWP has set aside $3 million and can expend more if needed from
  the Public Benefits account. GWP utilizes the same criteria as the federal CARES
  program.

  Commissioner Lall inquired about GWP’s ability to switch to remote and whether it was in
  part due to GWP having a disaster plan already in place before COVID-19. Ms. Vallier
  explained that GWP did have a disaster/emergency plan in place before COVID-19 to
  maintain services in the event of a “systems down” or other disasters (such as
  earthquakes).

c. Annual Water Quality Report.
  Mr. Michael De Ghetto, Chief Assistant General Manager, introduced Mr. James Saenz,
  Water Quality Manager, who presented the annual water quality report. Mr. Saenz
  provided a history of water quality analysis and provided an overview of the legislation
  governing water quality, such as the Federal Water Pollution Control Act of 1948, Clean
  Water Act of 1972, and Safe Drinking Water Act of 1974.

  Mr. Saenz summarized Glendale’s procedures and protocols to remain in compliance with
  all mandates. Mr. Saenz also discussed the Consumer Confidence Report and explained
  that it is available by July 1st of each year and can be found at GWP’s website, with hard
  copies available, which can be requested by calling GWP.

  Commissioner Flanigan thanked GWP staff for the report, especially the early history
  relating to water quality.

d. Scholl Biogas Project Update.
  Ms. Dorine Martirosian, Principal Assistant City Attorney, provided an update regarding
  the current status of the Scholl Biogas Project (and stated that the Draft Environmental
  Impact Report (DEIR) for the Project was released on July 2, 2020, for public review and
  comment, with the public comment period closing on September 30, 2020. Mr. Maurice
  Oillataguerre, Environmental Program Administrator, presented the Project and provided
  the Project history, including the previous Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) process,
  and explained that at the Planning Department's recommendation, GWP prepared the
  DEIR, which is currently published and undergoing the public comment period. Mr.
  Oillataguerre provided a proposed Project Timeline and stated that the public meetings
  before the Planning Commission and City Council are anticipated to occur in early 2021.
  Mr. Oillataguerre provided a project description of the four internal combustion engines to
  produce 12 megawatts of renewable energy using the landfill gas, the construction of
  60,000-gallon and 10,000-gallon water tanks, a new water main, and a new 2/3-mile
  natural gas makeup pipeline. Mr. Oillataguerre summarized the Project alternatives
  2
   analyzed in the DEIR, and the project alternatives considered and provided information on
  how and where the public can submit comments to the DEIR.

  Commissioner Flanigan commended GWP as one of the first utilities to have methane
  collection. He inquired about the poor gas quality (low methane and high levels of
  contaminants). Mr. Oillataguerre explained that the proposed internal combustion engines
  would be able to handle the landfill gas efficiently. Mr. Zurn explained that the proposed
  engines are designed to burn landfill gas, such as those generated at the City’s landfill.
  He further explained that turbines would not be able to function well with the landfill gas.
  Mr. Zurn further explained that upgrading the landfill gas quality to pipeline gas quality to
  use in the turbines would be very costly.

  Commissioner Lall inquired about the Project budget and output. Mr. Zurn stated that the
  Project budget is $30 million, and the output is 12 megawatts or 100% renewable
  electricity with zero transmission costs. Commissioner Lall inquired whether placing the
  engines at the Grayson Power Plant would be possible. Mr. Zurn explained that placing
  the engines at Grayson Power Plant would be a possibility; however, the emissions would
  be higher at Grayson Power Plant. Additionally, Mr. Zurn stated that there are more
  residences around the Grayson Power Plant, which would be affected by the higher
  emissions versus having the engines places at the landfill, which has more open land, and
  the residences are farther away.

  Commissioner Lall inquired whether the DEIR compared the emissions of the landfill gas
  burned in the engines to the landfill gas flared. Mr. Zurn and Mr. Oillataguerre stated that
  such a comparison is a part of the DEIR. Commissioner Lall inquired whether the GWP
  Commission will take any action relating to the DEIR and Project. Ms. Martirosian stated
  that the GWP Commission could make recommendations regarding the DEIR and Project.
  Commissioner Lall inquired about the estimated Project life span. Mr. Zurn stated that
  Project has an estimated life span of 20 years, perhaps even 30 to 40 years. Even though
  generations may decline as landfill gas levels decline, there will still be generation; Mr.
  Zurn provided an example of the closed portion of the Scholl Canyon Landfill and that
  while it closed in 1975, it still produces gas.

  Commissioner Flanigan inquired regarding the comparison between the flaring versus the
  internal combustion engines and whether there will be an answer to which one is cleaner.
  Mr. Zurn stated that there will be a clear answer and that SCAQMD regulations will
  mandate that GWP meet all requirements since SCAQMD guidelines apply to both flares
  and engines.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None.

6. AGENDA FORECAST
  The Commissioners reviewed and approved the agenda for the August 2020 meeting with
  the following changes:

  September 14, 2020 - Special Meeting: Clean Energy Alternatives report.
  October 5, 2020 - GWP Commission Elections (Secretary); Strategic Plan Update;
  Renewable Portfolio Update; Water Resources Update.
  November 2, 2020 - Legislative Update.
  December 7, 2020 - GWP Commission Elections (President and Secretary if Secretary not
  elected in October).
  3
   Commissioner Lall requested a report on the difference between power consumption before
  COVID-19 and after/because of COVID-19. She stated that it is important to see how the
  utility has pivoted and can respond in emergencies. Mr. Zurn noted that he would have this
  report presented to the Commission.

  Mr. Zurn also stated that GWP staff is in the process of researching and drafting an
  ordinance to ban the sale of Mylar Balloons within the City due to the damages caused to
  electric facilities when Mylar Balloons are released and come into contact with power lines
  and other related electric facilities, resulting in costly repairs and power outages to GWP
  customers.

7. ADJOURNMENT

  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Jazmadarian
  Seconded by: Commissioner Flanigan
  Motion Passed.
  The meeting was adjourned at 5:26 p.m.
